items.article: It's hard to fully love the misdirection of Digger but it's also something to see. See more of our coverage in your search results. For the better part of a year, the new Tom Cruise movie Digger has been sold on what is more or less a lie. The simple logline for a movie wouldn’t normally be worth quoting, but this one is notable for how the movie itself never really touches it. It’s supposedly about Cruise’s character Digger Rockwell as he “embarks on a frantic mission to prove that he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.” This sounds like a dark-comic flipside to Cruise’s work in the Mission: Impossible franchise , which ballooned from slick TV series remake to Cruise-and-director playground to, in its final installments , movies perhaps overly enraptured with the messianic can-do/will-do spirit of their death-defying star. In a sense, Digger is actually that: Dark Ethan Hunt, more concerned with the glory of his own money than the fate of the world. As such, the character never really goes on a “frantic mission” (possible or not) to save humanity. I prefer long-distance trains over any other form of travel because, unlike most things in my life, they force me to be still and enjoy the view. And even the most insufferable nights on the rails have helped me truly appreciate the great rides, like the one I took on a frosty day in January 2025. The California Zephyr runs from Chicago to San Francisco on Amtrak's Superliner fleet, which is two stories tall and comprises coach and first-class sleeper cars , as well as a dining car and an observation car. items.article: A record-breaking Super El Niño brewing in the Pacific Ocean is sending shockwaves through the global climate system Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. In a desperate bid to restore damaged coral reefs , scientists have turned to an unlikely solution – music. A record-breaking Super El Niño brewing in the Pacific Ocean is sending shockwaves through the global climate system, pushing sea surface temperatures to unprecedented heights and threatening ecosystems worldwide. The effects of this are severely hitting coral reefs – a vital marine ecosystem supporting a quarter of all sea life – which face catastrophic bleaching as rising water temperatures force them to expel their nutrient-providing algae. With heatwaves leaving ecosystems little time to naturally regenerate between repeat disasters, marine scientists are now scrambling to deploy radical new survival techniques. A project led by researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) in Massachusetts, and published in Royal Society Open Science, has found that sound can help preserve coral.

The money expert made the comments while sharing his thoughts on plans by Prime Minister Andy Burnham to scrap the so-called state pension triple lock. The triple lock guarantees the state pension rises annually by whichever is the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5 per cent, but is placing increasing pressure on UK public finances. On Tuesday, the PM pledged to reform the scheme into a double lock by removing the link to earnings. Now Martin Lewis , founder of the MoneySavingExpert website and a familiar face on both BBC and ITV , has set out what he believes the government must do next. And it hinges entirely on a benefit managed by the Department for Work and Pensions . In a post on X, he said: "If the triple lock on pensions will be scrapped. The 1st priority is to fix Pension Credit - the top up for the lowest earning pensioners to give them a basic minimum income. Shamefully many 100,000s of the poorest pensions still miss out on what they're entitled to." He has previously branded it a 'national tragedy' that so many eligible people fail to claim the benefit.
